title: Open meadow: fine mixed grass
notes: Olive ground with yellow-green blades, beige dry flecks, tiny stones and scattered low bushes. Fine texture remains irregular rather than forming a uniform fill.

title: Open meadow: quieter variation
notes: Quieter open ground with small exposed-earth patches and sparse stones. Useful density variation within the same grassy biome.

title: Stony grass: concentrated scree
notes: Loose gray and warm brown stones form an irregular concentration with grass visible between them; the patch has no hard perimeter.

title: Stony grass: dispersed stones
notes: Scattered pebble groups, pale exposed soil and small shrubs. A broader, less concentrated variant of the stony meadow.

title: Rock scatter and dry-grass detail
notes: Mixed stone sizes sit in rough yellow-green grass; dark contacts and pale upper faces make individual rocks legible.

title: Dense deciduous forest: broad mass
notes: Tightly overlapping rounded crowns, yellow-green upper-left highlights and very dark green interstices. Many crown sizes break up repetition.

title: Dense deciduous forest: repeated family
notes: A second broad forest mass with a scalloped border, small gaps and irregular crown heights; demonstrates variation within the same tree family.

title: Open woodland and grass corridors
notes: Detached clusters leave winding grass openings. The transition from forest to meadow is created by thinning crowns and small outlying shrubs.

title: Small isolated copse
notes: Compact asymmetrical group readable as several overlapping tree crowns, with a dark base and bright small canopy lobes.

title: Low bush clump beside the track
notes: A smaller, lower foliage mass gives scale variation between grass texture and full trees. Surrounding ground remains visible.

title: Forest fringe with detached crowns
notes: Trees gather into an uneven fringe above the shore, with detached crowns and grass gaps rather than a straight woodland boundary.

title: Small rocky knoll: pale shoulder
notes: Low grassy mound with one pale exposed rock shoulder, bushes at its foot and a shaded right slope.

title: Small rocky knoll: sharper crest
notes: A second small rise has a sharper stone crest and surrounding scrub. Grass wraps around the exposed rock instead of stopping at its edge.

title: Broad grassy hill with exposed faces
notes: Rounded stepped slopes, grassy ridgelines, gray-brown rock faces and deep green gullies. Upper-left light explains the volume.

title: Asymmetrical grassy massif
notes: A broad irregular hill with several rocky faces, bright ridges and dark planted slopes. Useful variation on the larger relief family.

title: Adjoining hills at the map edge
notes: Several connected grassy peaks show how relief can join into a chain. The source map boundary clips the leftmost forms.

title: Rounded isolated rise near a track
notes: A compact hill with a small gray crest and grass-covered shoulders, transitional in size between a rock outcrop and a broad hill.

title: Single crater and disturbed apron
notes: Irregular raised brown rim, radiating disturbed earth and a depressed olive-brown center. This reads as a crater rather than a trench.

title: Two craters with connected disturbed ground
notes: Differently sized adjacent depressions share an irregular bare-earth apron. Rim height, inner texture and outline vary between the two.

title: Crater close study: inner floor and rim
notes: Focused view of the dark inner rim, olive floor and cracked or rippled center. The source does not provide an explicit trench network or broad mud field.

title: Elongated crater variation
notes: The lower crater is more elongated and has a less regular rim, demonstrating useful shape variation without changing the material family.

title: Asphalt road: broad returning bend
notes: Gray paving, pale edge lines, dashed white center marking and warm gravel verges. The broad curve keeps an approximately consistent carriageway width.

title: Asphalt road: branching junction
notes: Connected paving at a branching junction; lane markings and shoulders adapt to the meeting roads. This is visibly modern marked asphalt.

title: Asphalt road: diagonal into vertical bend
notes: A long diagonal road turns toward a base entrance. Thin pale shoulder lines and exposed-earth margins separate the pavement from grass.

title: Road and dirt-track branching composition
notes: A curved paved road receives earth tracks at different points. The larger crop preserves the geometry and the contrasting surface widths.

title: Asphalt material and verge detail
notes: Focused diagonal strip showing gray pavement, dashed center line, pale continuous edges, warm shoulder and immediately adjacent grass.

title: Earth track: diagonal approach
notes: Thin ochre route with two worn ruts and an irregular grassy center. Soft margins blend into the meadow; no painted markings.

title: Earth track: winding meadow route
notes: Curving worn-earth path with slight width and color changes, bordered by grass and small plants.

title: Earth track: paved-road transition
notes: The dirt route branches from the paved surface. Worn brown ground broadens at the junction and narrows into the meadow.

title: Earth track: paired-rut detail
notes: Focused near-vertical track segment showing two light worn bands, a darker or grassy center and irregular plant growth along both sides.

title: River bend beside the northern compound
notes: Dark teal water, cyan facets and many short white ripples. Pale boulders tightly line an irregular bank, with grass and bushes immediately beyond.

title: Lake with rock islands and irregular shore
notes: Broad water surface uses the same teal-and-white ripple language as the river. A pale rocky shoreline encloses the lake and four rocks break the surface.

title: Narrow creek and asymmetric banks
notes: Richly textured water remains visible through a narrow curving channel. Banks have asymmetric rocks, grass projections and nearby woodland.

title: Rocky bank: water-to-grass transition
notes: Mixed pale gray and tan boulders, dark contact shadows, a thin warm soil margin and immediate green vegetation connect water to land.

title: Four water rocks: size variations
notes: Four differently sized exposed rocks have pale crowns and dark bases, with bright ripples around them. Keep this as a repeated-detail reference.

title: Water close study: overlapping bright ripples
notes: Open-water detail shows short white and cyan strokes over a darker teal field. The conspicuous ripple density is a specific visual choice in this source.

title: Detached huts and ancillary boxes
notes: Two small brown and tan huts with pitched or pyramidal roofs, compact wall footprints and dark right-side shadows; small detached boxes accompany them.

title: Isolated hut beside the southern track
notes: A repeated small hut in a different setting, useful for separating the roof, tiny walls, nearby box and ground shadow from compound scenery.

title: Service compound: complete central installation
notes: Fenced compact compound with an emblem-marked central building, small huts, red-accent shed and bright white tank- or shed-like objects in green frames. Exact equipment identities are ambiguous.

title: Service compound: repeated southern installation
notes: A near-duplicate compound confirms a reusable structure family. Keep the full composition to study spacing, fence, entrance and adjacent grass.

title: Fortified industrial compound: northern example
notes: Four bright metallic corner assemblies connect around a square; red gate roofs and a central passage contrast with deep structural shadows.

title: Fortified industrial compound: southern repetition
notes: Repeated four-corner installation with red-roofed entrance elements, bright cylindrical-looking components and dark connecting members.

title: Short diagonal bridge over the lake outlet
notes: Narrow gray-tan diagonal deck crosses the outlet, with contrasting edge strips. Includes both abutments and nearby rocky banks.

title: Long north-south bridge over the creek
notes: Pale slab deck with darker longitudinal edges spans the creek. The complete crossing shows land contacts on both banks.

title: Northern road crossing through the river bend
notes: The asphalt crosses the upper river near the vertical road. Separate deck boundaries are subtle; the white cross-road bar farther south may be an entrance gantry.

title: White cross-road entrance gantry
notes: A slim white bar spans the road immediately before the service compound. It reads as a checkpoint or base entrance rather than a water bridge; classification remains tentative.

title: Circular marker beside a hut
notes: White-outlined circular symbol appears beside a hut. Treat as a gameplay or interface marker, not terrain or a building material.

title: Repeated red tabs along the lower boundary
notes: Red diamond-like tabs with white bars and small central icons overlap the bottom edge. These are interface elements rather than landscape features.
